tools.name: fill_template
tools.title: Fill a report template into a new file
tools.description: Fill a report template of this conversation into a new file; the template itself is not changed, and a .dotx becomes a .docx. A slide master (.pptx or .potx) is not filled with this: build a deck in it with write_presentation. Call inspect_template first and agree the values with the user. values maps each field's name to its value and its source, and every value needs a source: kind file (the path of a file of this conversation as list_files gives it, with page for a PDF page or PPTX slide, or sheet and cell such as B7 for a workbook), job (the job_id of the run_python run that computed it: every computed figure cites its job_id), user (the user said it; note says where) or assistant (you wrote it). Types: text and rich_text take a string or a number, date YYYY-MM-DD, dropdown one of its options, checkbox true or false, table a list of rows (each a list of values in a workbook). Fields without a value are listed in unfilled. The new file ends with a Sources table (a Sources sheet in a workbook) naming each value's source; include_sources false leaves it out. The user sees the new file as a card in the chat.

tools.name: inspect_template
tools.title: List the fields of a template or the layouts of a slide master
tools.description: List the fields of a report template in this conversation, so you can plan the fill with the user before you call fill_template. Templates are Word .docx and .dotx files with content controls or legacy form fields, Word .docx files with {{ field }} placeholders (loops and conditions too), and Excel .xlsx files with {{ field }} cells and {{ table:name }} cells where a table grows downwards. Each field has its name (give its value under it), kind, type (text, rich_text, date, dropdown with its options, checkbox, table) and location. template_kind none means version 1 cannot fill the file: tell the user what it needs, as hint says. PowerPoint .pptx and .potx files are slide masters: their layouts are listed, numbered, with each layout's places in reading order (role, about how many lines and characters fit) and whether it has a footer; build a deck in one with write_presentation. Without path, it lists the layouts of the plain 16:9 master write_presentation uses when the user gave none. A very long list is cut: truncated is then true.

tools.name: read_document
tools.title: Read a file of this conversation as text
tools.description: Read one file of this conversation as text, each piece with a reference. Readable: PDF, DOCX, DOTX, XLSX, XLSM, CSV, TSV, PPTX, POTX, ODT, ODS, EML, HTML, JSON (shown indented), JSONL, NDJSON, TXT and MD, and pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF, HEIC), which come back as the image. Give the file's path from list_files. Reading starts at part (the start if left out) and goes on until the result limit, so a long file is read in several calls: when truncated is true, call again with part set to next_part. Parts are pages ('page 3', 'pages 3-9'), slides ('slide 2'), paragraphs ('paragraph 40'), runs of table rows ('table 2, rows 30-60'; a search location such as 'table 2, row 350' opens there), ranges of up to 200 sheet rows ('Sheet1!A201:F400', each line 'row: cell | cell'; a sheet's name starts at its first row) and lines ('lines 100-200'). Cite what you read by these references. pages_without_text lists pages or slides with no text layer (scans, pictures); never treat them as blank. Such PDF pages and PowerPoint slides come back as images in the same answer (shown names them): read them from the images. To look at any page or slide, use view_file. Outlook .msg files cannot be read: ask the user to save them as .eml or PDF.

tools.name: run_python
tools.title: Run Python on the files of this conversation
tools.description: Run Python code on this conversation's files and get back what it printed. The files are in the current folder, under their names as list_files gives them (also at their /workspace/<chat>/<name> paths), read-only. Write every result file directly into the out/ folder, not into a subfolder: each becomes a new file of the workspace, and files lists their paths (at most 20 files a run). Save charts as image files there, for example plt.savefig('out/chart.png'); nothing is shown inline, so the user sees each file in out/ as a card in the chat. Installed: pandas, numpy, scipy, matplotlib, openpyxl, xlsxwriter, python-docx, docxtpl, python-pptx, pypdf, odfpy, lxml, beautifulsoup4, pillow, pypdfium2. To turn a data file (JSON, CSV, XLSX) into a table file, load it in code (json, pandas.json_normalize) and write it to out/ as .xlsx or .csv; do not copy its rows into write_table. There is no network and nothing can be installed. Use threads, not multiprocessing: process pools and multiprocessing do not work here. The code runs as a script with a time limit; an error or timeout is in stderr. stdout and stderr are cut in the middle when long (truncated is then true), so print summaries, not whole tables. Cite job_id as the source of figures the code computed.

tools.name: write_presentation
tools.title: Build a slide deck in a slide master
tools.description: Build a PowerPoint deck into a new .pptx of this conversation, in a slide master (.pptx or .potx) of it. Without path, the deck is built in a plain 16:9 master. Call inspect_template on the master first (without path for the plain one). Then show the user the outline (each slide's title, layout number and name, key points, figures and sources) and call this tool only in a later message, after they agreed. Each content entry fills one place of the slide's layout, in the order inspect_template lists its places: Markdown text (bullets with -, up to 3 levels, **bold**, *italic*), {table: rows} with the first row the header, {chart: {type, categories, series}}, or {image: path} of a PNG, JPEG or GIF of this conversation (make a chart image with run_python, or prefer a native chart); "" leaves a place empty. A slide's title and subtitle are plain text, not Markdown. At most 30 slides. Footers and slide numbers come from the master; the master's own slides are left out. Each slide's sources go into its speaker notes. View the new deck with view_file. To change it, read it with read_document and write it again, or restyle it in run_python. The user sees the new file as a card in the chat.

tools.name: write_table
tools.title: Write a table into a new Excel or CSV file
tools.description: Write a table into a new file of this conversation: an Excel workbook (format xlsx, a bold header row that stays in view) or a CSV file (format csv, UTF-8, comma-separated unless delimiter is ; or a tab). For people who will open the file in Excel, use xlsx: Excel reads a CSV file by the computer's regional settings (German Excel splits it on ; and may read 1.5 as text or a date), so CSV is for exchanging data with other programs. columns are the header's names; rows are lists of values in the columns' order, each a string, a number, true, false or null; a shorter row is filled with empty cells. At most 100000 rows, 16384 columns and 32767 characters a cell. Values are data, never formulas: =SUM(A1:A3), 0042 or a web address stay text; a number keeps 15 significant digits in Excel, so write long identifiers as strings. In a CSV a text that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading ' so that a spreadsheet does not run it, and hint says how many. sheet names the workbook's sheet. One request is at most 1 MB: for a large table, write the file with run_python into out/ instead. The user sees the new file as a card in the chat.
